description: Figure 5, titled “The average likes of headlines from different season groups,” is a bar chart that displays the average number of likes received by headlines grouped by season. The horizontal axis categorizes the data into five distinct time intervals labeled as “(0,90]”, “(90,180]”, “(180,270]”, “(270,360]”, and “(360,450]”, which likely represent day ranges relative to a reference point (e.g., days since a seasonal start). The vertical axis, labeled “Avg. Like #”, is scaled from 400 to 600 in increments of 50, indicating the average number of likes per headline group. Each bar corresponds to one of the five day intervals and is colored light blue with vertical error bars extending above and below the bar, representing the standard deviation or standard error of the mean. The heights of the bars show that headlines in the earliest interval, “(0,90]”, receive the highest average likes (approximately 540), followed by a general downward trend across subsequent intervals, with the “(360,450]” group showing the lowest average likes (around 520). The chart visually suggests that headlines posted earlier in the seasonal cycle tend to garner more engagement on average.
